title: Wraiths
summary: The Restless Dead: souls held back from what lies beyond by unfinished business.

claims.text: Everyone dies with something left undone; for a few it is enough to hold them near the world instead of moving on.
Some wraiths stay near the living and haunt them; others go deeper into the Underworld.
Wraiths call themselves the Restless.

title: The Shadowlands and the Skinlands
summary: The lands of the dead lying over the world of the living.

claims.text: The Shadowlands lie over the living Skinlands like a sheer blanket, full of memories and echoes such as fallen buildings and old roads.
Ghosts with strong Fetters often dwell there.

title: The Shroud
summary: The barrier between the living and the dead.

claims.text: The Shroud is a membrane of fear and disbelief between the Shadowlands and the living world.
Through it the dead can see the living, but it keeps them from touching that world.
A great convulsion in the distant past tore the realms apart and raised the Shroud.

title: The Sundering
summary: The ancient rift that split the living from the dead.

claims.text: Long ago, for reasons no one knows, a great upheaval split the land of the dead from the land of the living.

title: Oblivion
summary: The void that waits to swallow the dead.

claims.text: Oblivion is the eternal void, one of the fates that may follow death.
The Shadow seeks to edge its wraith toward Oblivion.

title: Transcendence
summary: The hope of rising to a higher state beyond the Underworld.

claims.text: Some of the Restless hope for Transcendence, an ascent to a higher state, and strive for it without end.
They disagree among themselves about how it is won.

title: The Shadow
summary: The dark half of every wraith, bent on its destruction.

claims.text: The Shadow is the part of a wraith bent on self-destruction, with a malign life of its own inside the wraith's mind.
It bribes, coaxes, threatens and sometimes seizes control.
Angst is the dark mental energy the Shadow and Spectres feed on; the Psyche is the brighter side that looks past self-destruction.

title: Catharsis
summary: When the Shadow takes the wraith's body.

claims.text: When the Psyche weakens, the Shadow can take temporary control of the Corpus; the dead call this Catharsis.
A Catharsis may last seconds and seldom lasts longer than a few hours.

title: Passions and Fetters
summary: What a wraith feels most, and what holds it to the world.

claims.text: Passions are the strong feelings and purposes that drive a wraith; acting on them yields Pathos.
Fetters are what a wraith feels most strongly about: loved ones, treasured places, tools of satisfying work, or hated reminders of old losses.
A Fetter can be ruined by chance as well as by enemies; even a tower is lost if an earthquake fells it.

title: Pathos
summary: The energy of raw emotion that sustains the dead.

claims.text: Pathos is pure emotional energy that wraiths feed on and use to sustain themselves.
A wraith gains Pathos by following its Passions.

title: Corpus
summary: A wraith's body in the Underworld.

claims.text: The Corpus is made of plasm, the raw stuff of the afterlife, rather than living tissue.
In skilled hands, such as a Masquer's, plasm can be reshaped endlessly.

title: The Caul
summary: The sheath that wraps a newly dead soul.

claims.text: A new wraith wakes wrapped in an ectoplasmic Caul that blurs the senses and binds movement.
Some never escape the Caul and linger on lost.

title: Reaping
summary: The hunt for newly dead souls.

claims.text: Older wraiths call the search for new souls Reaping.
Some reapers want Thralls, souls bound as slaves or prisoners; others want raw material for the soulforges.

title: Deathmarks
summary: The marks of death and afterlife carried on every Corpus.

claims.text: Every Corpus bears marks of the wraith's life and death, caused by trauma and some Arcanoi.
Vain or subversive wraiths try to sculpt them away.

title: Masks
summary: The masks of office worn in the Hierarchy.

claims.text: Masks are optional in the Hierarchy, yet any wraith with ambition there wears one.
Masks can be symbols of office, expressions of self, or items of power.

title: Soulforging
summary: Melting souls into objects.

claims.text: A subject's Corpus is heated over soulfire crystals until it softens, then hammered into shape.
Soulfire crystals are shards a master Usurer has charged with Pathos.

title: Oboli
summary: The coin of Stygia.

claims.text: Oboli are the only coinage accepted everywhere in Stygia, though some Necropoli take other relic money.
The coins are heavy for their size.

title: Charon
summary: The ferryman of Mycenae who became the first ruler of the dead.

claims.text: The Lady of Fate foretold a leader who would come down the River of Death and guide the souls.
That leader, Charon, rose from among the dead of Mycenae.
Charon founded the Republic of Stygia on the model of the Roman Republic, with a Senate.

title: The Lady of Fate
summary: The prophet who foresaw Charon and still watches over Stygia.

claims.text: In the chaos of the Underworld the Lady of Fate foretold a great leader.
While others faded over the centuries, the Lady endures and watches over the order helped into being.
The Lady urged Charon down into the Labyrinth to face Oblivion.

title: Stygia
summary: The great city and empire of the dead.

claims.text: Charon set up the first government of the dead as the Republic of Stygia.
The Midnight Express, a ghostly train, calls at many Necropoli on its way down into the deep Underworld.

title: The Great Maelstroms
summary: The storms of the Underworld that shake the realm of the dead.

claims.text: The First Great Maelstrom came with a roar from the Labyrinth, and Charon's sentries rang gongs to warn the dead.
The Fifth Great Maelstrom shook the Labyrinth loose and freed the Malfean Gorool.

title: The Hierarchy and the Legions
summary: Stygia's ruling order, built on eight Legions.

claims.text: The Legions are the framework of the Hierarchy, as Rome's legions were for Republic and Empire.
Every wraith belongs, in principle, to one of eight Legions, assigned on arrival.
Each Legion answers to a Deathlord, with ranks like those of the Roman legions.

title: Renegades
summary: Wraiths who oppose Stygia for worldly reasons.

claims.text: Opponents of Stygia with political aims are called Renegades; religious ones, Heretics.
Both are many small groups that may share as little with each other as with Stygia.

title: Heretics
summary: The cults and creeds of the dead.

claims.text: A real afterlife did not end arguments over religion among the dead.
The Legions crack down hard on Heretic cults that recruit among Stygia's poor.

title: The Ferrymen
summary: Wraiths who cut out their own Shadows.

claims.text: In the Severance a Ferryman's Shadow is cut from the Corpus and lives on as a separate Spectre, a Pasiphae.
After the Severance a Ferryman cannot suffer Catharsis.

title: The Guilds
summary: Part trade cartel, part secret society, each built around an Arcanos.

claims.text: The Guilds formed around the practice of particular Arcanoi, modelled on living trade guilds.
Guild members are the masters of their arts and guard the path to advanced study.
The Mnemoi, who work on memory, are the most reviled Guild, once Stygia's trusted judges.

title: Arcanoi
summary: The powers of the dead.

claims.text: An Arcanos lets a wraith affect the living and the dead; the plural is Arcanoi.

title: Spectres
summary: Wraiths whose Shadows have won.

claims.text: Spectres feed on Angst as the Shadow does; in a Spectre the Psyche takes the place a Shadow holds in a wraith.
